Spend time with shelter cats

Cats don't usually go on outings. New places stress them out. But there are still great ways to give a shelter cat a break and help them get adopted.

Ways to help shelter cats

Staycations and sleepovers. Some shelters let you take an adult cat home for a night or a few days. The cat gets a quiet break, and the shelter learns how they act in a home.

Cat lounges and cafés. Rescue-run lounges let you hang out with adoptable cats and kittens for an hour or more. Your admission helps fund their care.

Kitten fostering. In spring and summer, shelters need homes for very young kittens for a few weeks. Ask your local shelter about its foster program.

ShelterDayOut is a free directory. We don't run outings or handle bookings; each shelter sets its own rules. Listings are checked monthly, but details change, so confirm with the shelter before you go.

Ready to adopt? ShelterAdoption, our sister site, lists every shelter near you plus upcoming adoption events.
